title: The Subordinates’ Pleasure
text: “Alright, big sis! Let’s get the Spear Hero to down one more before we crack open another bottle!”
“You bet!”

Glug, glug—more sake poured into my cup. Ngh… I can still manage, but the drunkenness is starting to catch up to me, I say. Somehow I managed to drink it down and set the cup on the table. Any more than this would be pushing it, I say. I’d fall over drunk.
“Big sis!”
“Aye-aye! Glug! Glug!”
Panda, apparently still not satisfied, drained the cup and slammed it down onto the table with a bang. Then she smacked her head against the table and… had she suddenly passed out drunk?
“Hic… hnnnn?”
She lifted her head, eyes unfocused. Were those eyes even properly seated in their sockets?
“Hey, you lot! Listen to what I’ve got to say!”
“Yes, ma’am!”
“Right you are, ma’am!”
“You two as well!”
Panda turned her sharp gaze on us as well.
“A-ah”
“Er…”
“Indeed, I say…”
The drunkenness was starting to muddle my thoughts, I say. Panda, whatever could you possibly want to talk about?
“Listen up! Right now, I am—super! Happy!”

…Panda broke into an utterly blissful, melting grin. What was this? I’d expected some kind of complaint given the mood, but her face looked happier than I’d ever seen it. Still… I vaguely recalled having seen Panda in this state before. If memory serves, it was around the time Father—having given his body over to Rival—was carrying a dead-drunk Panda over his shoulder. I’d seen this side of Panda once before, back when we’d returned to Siltvelt between legs of our journey.

“You know that Shield guy? He looked at every single one of my true feelings, my real thoughts, all of it—and he never once laughed and said I was weird. And he even called me cute! He’d hand me all these clothes and accessories, and even when I said things I didn’t mean, like ‘this doesn’t suit me,’ he’d just force me to put it on anyway and then praise me for it, and it made me so, so happy!”
“……I see.”
Faced with the strange silence—or rather, Panda’s rambling—all we could do was nod along.

“And Sadeena, that woman’s crazy strong, and crazy good at drinking too, and the two of them are dating now—ugh… I was after him too, you know, but I tried to hide it and she still figured it out! Seriously, her instincts are too sharp! I got swept along with it, but I don’t regret it one bit! He treats me plenty good too! No need to hog him all to myself, right?!”
…Her entire personality had completely changed, this Panda.

“And then, you know, there was that time I had a kid in my belly and got all irritable and took it out on everyone, but he just said he didn’t mind and forgave me, and he even went and looked into it properly for me. The baby was born safe and sound, and he understood how hard childcare is and pitched in to help, so I’m gonna do my best too!”
“I see… good luck with that.”
“……Yes, do your best.”

“And you, Sword boy—you’ve had it rough in all sorts of ways, but I get it, you know, a hero who saved the world and all that. Probably had plots against you and your life threatened more times than I can count, but I’ll give you your praise! And you did work in the culinary field too, right? I heard about it, you know!”
Panda patted Ren’s head like he was a good little boy and gave him a light hug.
“Even technique-wise, you’ve apparently grown to where you’re almost on par with the lady knight, right? So impressive!”
“Ah… ah.”
When Ren nodded, Panda turned to face Itsuki and leaned in close.

“And you, Bow boy, you’ve had it tough too, and on top of that you’ve got Fleon and that Rafuemon fellow with you, right? Looking after your companions is hard work, but it’s definitely worth doing, so see it through! Oh, and that Rishia girl, she’s a smart one—talk to her a little and you can tell. That girl’s a gem, don’t you dare let her slip away!”
“Th-thank you very much…”
“And I know you play a mean tune on that instrument of yours! Fighting isn’t everything in life. That talent of yours is one of a kind, so be proud of it!”
And so she praised both Ren and Itsuki like that. Now it was my turn—or so I thought, but before that, one of Panda’s subordinates raised his hand.
“Big sis! How about me?”

“Ah? You’ve been working hard alongside those two lately too, haven’t you! I heard how the folks in the country were grateful because you put real effort into the calculations! Good boy! You’re a subordinate I’m proud of!”
And with that, Panda pulled the subordinate who’d raised his hand into a hug, cooing at him like a good boy, and started petting his head.
“Big sis! My turn now!”

“What do you mean, ‘your turn’? Honestly. Well, you brought in a nice haul of game the other day. And lately your footwork’s gotten sharper, your hands are getting better too. Try your debut in the Colosseum next time! I bet you’ll go places!”
“Thank you very much, ma’am!”
Panda’s subordinates kept clamoring “Me too, me too!”, jockeying for Panda’s praise, their spirits climbing higher and higher.
“What in the world is this…”
“This right here is exactly why we follow big sis.”
One of Panda’s subordinates grinned wickedly and began explaining to Itsuki.

“Big sis looks after us real well, she’s crazy strong, and you can always count on her—plenty of us have joined up as her subordinates over the years. But when she gets stone drunk like this, she praises us to the skies like you just saw. Thinking that’s her real, honest feelings gets us all fired up something fierce.”
“So she’s a compliment-drunk, is that it…”
“And on top of that, she gets all lovey-dovey about her man in front of everyone. So we all call her the ‘love-drunk.’”
“Doesn’t it feel hollow, getting her drunk on purpose just to hear that?”
“If you ask her the finer details, she’ll tell you straight where you’re falling short too, no fuss about it. So it’s a real learning experience, and it lights a fire under you.”
“……I see.”
Panda went around hugging each subordinate in turn, showering them all with a good little boy treatment.
“Actually, I feel like I’m seeing this for the first time…”
“She hardly ever gets this stone drunk. Even when she does get drunk, this particular state only shows up maybe one time in five.”
“And all of you subordinates are aiming for that rare occurrence, hm… Though I’d think plenty of mischief could be gotten up to while she’s in that state.”
“Don’t say something so dangerous, Bow Hero-sama.”
Panda’s subordinate went pale and trembled all over.

“There was a good-for-nothing among our ranks once, way back—tried to do something improper to big sis while she was in that state. Turns out, if you try anything funny with her like that, she goes berserk and turns downright savage. That fool got his whole head bitten clean, torn to shreds by claws, and squeezed so hard it was a real disaster. Took a lot of work cleaning up that mess afterward.”

He even went so far as to say: “It’s enviable that the Shield brat ended up bound to big sis, but that means she opened her heart to him. Nobody less impressive than the Shield Hero would ever be a match for her. None of us could ever stand shoulder to shoulder with someone of her caliber.”

“It’s the most blessed, the finest moment for us subordinates. Between those gentle words and her strict-yet-kind guidance day to day, that’s why we all adore big sis so much. By the way, big sis has no memory of this state whatsoever.”
“I’ve come to understand that your camaraderie is rather twisted.”
“That’s uncalled for. We’d do anything for big sis’s happiness and well-being, day in and day out, and if anything ever happened, we’d come running and lay down our lives for her without hesitation.”

“I understand you mean to say it’s an unbreakable bond of loyalty, but… well, considering Larsazusa-san’s Demi-Human form is that of a big-sisterly beauty, I suppose it makes sense you’d all end up like this under her guidance. Just—please don’t try to recruit us as subordinates.”
“Can’t be helped, then.”
“We’ll invite Fohl to the next drinking party too. He’s sure to become one of us.”
Ah, right, I recalled seeing that. Since he’d joined in on the coordination before, I suppose they’d get along.

“So Fohl-san is joining Larsazusa-san’s subordinate alliance too… I’m not sure if that counts as the same category as our brainwashed ranks, so let’s hear more later and decide whether he needs rescuing. Ren-san.”
“Yeah… I won’t forget Motoyasu’s sacrifice. Even if he’s not Naofumi, he made for a fine shield for the rest of us.”
“It’s a relief that we can’t drink alcohol, isn’t it.”
Ren and Itsuki were saying whatever selfish things came to mind, watching me slump over, drunk out of my mind.
“Uughhh…”

Should I make a scene right about now? But no—this Motoyasu, with his iron-clad mental fortitude, avoids drunken rampages, I say. And so, that day, we entrusted the dead-drunk Panda to her subordinates and headed back to the village ahead of everyone else, I say.
One day.
“A request to serve as an instructor at the magic academy affiliated with Faubrey?”
Éclair came by one evening while we were all gathered eating dinner together at the village dining hall, bringing this proposal to us.

“Indeed… apparently the proposal comes from the leadership of various nations, Faubrey chief among them. They’d like the Four Cardinal Heroes, who brought peace to the world, to serve as instructors. It seems the worldwide chaos has largely settled down at this point.”
“The magic academy had suspended classes ever since the disaster of the Waves struck during the long break at the turn of the school year, and now it’s set to reopen…”

Fiancée seemed to have come representing a similar request from the country regarding this matter. And apparently, Elephant had received the same request as well, with both nations making the same ask—all three of them stood before us now, wearing troubled expressions as they made the proposal.
“I believe it’s possible to decline, but… they’d very much like you to accept, if at all possible.”
“Instructors, huh… The question is whether we know enough magic to actually teach people—”
“Isn’t it probably that thing? There’s magic only heroes can use, after all, so it’s probably instructor duty combined with hero research, that sort of thing.”
“That’s plausible. Though there’s likely some other angle to it as well…”

So there were requests like this too, I see. Oh? Come to think of it, I feel like there was a similar request in one of the previous loops as well. Most likely it was one of those requests Father told me not to worry about, and I never got involved with it.
“There are surely various ulterior motives at play, but the gist is that people want to hear directly from you heroes.”
“If it’s just about teaching magic, seems like it could be handled by folks other than us, though.”
Ren said this while glancing at Rival and Older Sister and the others. His gaze drifted toward Assistant as well, incidentally.
“You’ve been named specifically as the Four Cardinal Heroes. I doubt Gaelion-dono or Sadeena-dono and the others would receive a warm welcome if they went instead.”
Éclair, in her roundabout way, was conveying that it wasn’t possible to simply push the job off onto Rival and the others.
“Hmm… even if we turn it down here, seems like the King of Faubrey or someone would probably bring it up again anyway…”
“The likelihood is extremely high. That’s how many people apparently want lessons from the heroes who saved the world—there are that many.”
“So no matter how much we refuse, we’ll eventually have to do it regardless, huh… If we refuse carelessly, we’ll probably just end up with an even more troublesome request coming our way.”
Father muttered quietly to himself something about how Faubrey and the other nations had done plenty of favors for us already…
“So it’s the Four Cardinal Heroes, meaning all of us?”
“No, there’s no such specific requirement. They’d like just one of you to be stationed at the academy full-time for a while.”
“So they’ve at least shown some consideration on that front, huh…”
Hmm… Father and the others groaned, mulling it over.
“For now, I guess we’ll rotate through, but the question is who goes first to be stationed there.”
“Yes, that’s how it’ll shake out.”
“The problem is who goes first, though…”
Ren and Itsuki kept glancing back and forth at each other.
“Bow Hero would be the safest choice here, nano.”
Rival casually tossed out this suggestion.
“Eh? Itsuki’s the one going? Ah, I see!”
“H-hold—”
Father’s eyes began sparkling, and Ren seemed to be falling right in line with him too. I suppose I’ll join in as well.
“Rafuemon!”
“With Itsuki!”
“At the magic academy, I say!”
A vein bulged on Itsuki’s forehead as he clenched his fist.
“Y-you people! Are you planning to spout nonsense about the movie version or something?!”
“Eh? Um… Itsuki-kun. I’ll help out too, okay?”
“No, Rafuemon-san, please don’t worry about it. In fact, please don’t come at all—you’ll probably just end up material for Naofumi-san and the others’ jokes.”
“Th-that so? But I’m worried, Itsuki-kun…”
Rafuemon really did seem to be the anxious type.
“Setting aside Naofumi-san and the others’ nonsense, Gaelion-san… I suppose I’ll ask your reasoning, just this once.”
Itsuki asked warily, brow furrowed.
“Rival, what’s your angle here, I say?”

“Simply speaking in terms of who’s suited and who isn’t, nano. Naofumi has some free time, sure, but he’s got the kids to look after and plenty to do around the village too, nano. And besides, his aptitude leans toward recovery and support magic, so what he could actually teach is limited, nano.”

“That’s certainly true. In Naofumi-san’s case, he can handle wound treatment and physical enhancement, but the range of magic he can actually use is limited. He’d probably be good at teaching, though.”

“Hearing that put like that stings a little. Since it’s a magic school, the students can obviously already read and write, and this kind of class would surely need to cover offensive magic too, right?”
Everyone figured he’d be well-suited for a medical department, but going first meant he was too specialized for the job.
“Next up is the Sword Hero, but needless to say, he’s terrible at speaking in front of large crowds and isn’t suited for it, nano.”
“Ah… yeah.”
“Ren gets shy around people, I say!”

“If anything, he’d probably come across as condescending right off the bat and get misunderstood. He’d likely end up needlessly resented by some noble’s son who isn’t even a reincarnator. Though I suppose if he just let them have it and things worked out, he might end up creating an elite specialized class as a result.”
“Shut up!”
Certainly, Ren did have a bit of a quirky teaching style. And the concern that he might end up teaching swordsmanship at a magic school instead was a valid one, I say.
“And as for the Spear Hero, he’s out of the question entirely, nano.”
